More important than the actual ratio of non-whites to whites, is the trends indicated by Census information for years 1960 to 1970. The above percentages given for the two Census tracts, covering the south and north ends of the project, were from the most recent 1970 Census. The 1960 Census indicated percentages of 0.1 for the south end and 10.5 for the north end--respective increases of 4,400 percent and 134 percent.
This trend will probably continue over the coming year due to the pressure from the almost totally non-white areas (90.4 percent) directly east of the project across 5th street.
g. Citizens Participation
Prior to the development of the proposed urban renewal application, there were no known active community organizations in the specific project area. A Project Area Committee (P. A. C.) had been formed as a result of the Activities in the Hamilton N. D. P. Area.
The subject project has now formed its own P. A. C., selected its officers and has held a number of meetings in connection with the development of the final draft of the urban renewal application. The project residents, represented by the Project Area Committee, have been deeply involved in the decision making process in the development of the application (see Part IV for dates the Committee met; also, see the "Synopsis" in Part I for statistics on composition of the Committee.)
The second P. A. C. meeting held drew more than 300 project residents, some of whom were living in temporary housing outside of the project area at the time. This is an indication that there is an active community spirit in the area and that the projects residents are vitally interested in rebuilding their area.
The Project Area Committee will continue to function during the execution stages of the project. Its activities will, in part, be funded at project expense.
